readout_other: local field potential (sharp wave ripples in slices; theta oscillations in intact hippocampus)
direction_notes: No set of parameters produced detectable effects on sharp wave ripple amplitude, interval or ripple frequency in slices, nor on theta oscillation amplitude or frequency in the intact rat hippocampus, with or without 5 uM nicotine.

timing.protocol_description: Brief single pulses (0.5-20 ms) repeated at 200-700 ms intervals for 5 min, flanked by 5 min control recordings; tone bursts (e.g. 50 ms burst, 200 Hz PRF, 0.5 or 1 ms pulses) tested in two slices and a 5 s stimulus in one slice.
2 s continuous-wave ultrasound repeated every 20 s for 5 min, also repeated with 5 uM nicotine in the bath.

source_quotes.n_subjects: A detailed breakdown of the stimulus conditions and results for all seven slices tested is provided in Fig. 5, which shows the mean interevent interval (as determined from the log-normal distribution fit) as a function of trial number for all control and ultrasound trials.

source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_duration_ms: The repeated ultrasound stimulus was a brief (0.5–20 ms pulse duration) ultrasound application at 1 MHz, with pressure ranging from 100 to 600 kPa, repeated with a pulse repetition interval of 200–700 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: To test these hypotheses, and to examine ultrasound’s effects in another system, we measured the effects of ultrasound on theta oscillations in the intact rat hippocampus in vitro. We found that ultrasound at 1 MHz and 500 kPa, applied continuously for 2 s, produced no detectable effects on the amplitude or frequency of in vitro theta oscillations.

source_quotes.exposures[1].timing.sonication_duration_: For SWR exper iments, ultrasound was applied with a range of pressures, pulse durations, and pulse repetition intervals as summarized in the results. For theta oscillation experiments, ultrasound was applied at 500 kPa with a pulse duration of 2 s and a pulse repetition interval of 20 s.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.pulse_repetition_fre: The repeated ultrasound stimulus was a brief (0.5–20 ms pulse duration) ultrasound application at 1 MHz, with pressure ranging from 100 to 600 kPa, repeated with a pulse repetition interval of 200–700 ms.
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: In all experiments, the ultrasound stimulus was repeated for 5 min, flanked by 5-min of control recording without ultrasound stimulation.
